newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds soften with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds soften with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds were flat to lower late Friday as the market fell with U.S. Treasuries in response to rising worries over more U.S. rate hikes.

"The next move by the U.S. Federal Reserve will be fundamental" to the Argentine market, said one trader, referring to the session's U.S. jobless report which had many analysts thinking another rate hike is likely.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 3/8 at 89-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was flat at 127.10.
Another trader said that with the employment report not having settled the uncertainty surrounding U.S. rates, activity could well remain thin next week.
He added that the Argentine market is now dominated by traders as investors remain on the sidelines awaiting a clearer outlook.
Some players suggested the market could well trade sideways at least until the Federal Reserve next meets in May.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.03 percent from 6.35 percent.
